svg.title: MCP step-up mid-interaction: 403 insufficient_scope + hold-and-replay (with pre-step-up elicitation, pending operation and operation-bound scope)

g.text: (with pre-step-up elicitation, pending operation and operation-bound scope)
the SDK has not seen the 401
The standalone GET stream is what carries the elicitation later:
in JSON response mode the POST has no stream for server→client requests.
1. Tool call that turns out to need more authorization
Only now does the tool know that the
The SDK resolves the transport Response with an isError
result; the HTTP layer DISCARDS it and rewrites to 403.
Rule: 4xx ⇒ nothing executed for this request.
4. Client-side step-up (request id=7 is HELD, LLM unaware)
The AS only knows the scope string, not the payment details.
RAR authorization_details would let it render
op_X stays awaiting_step_up until TTL → failed.
5. Replay: same HTTP request, resumed from checkpoint
7. Next high-risk operation: operation-bound token does not carry over
repeat phases 4-5 for op_Y (fresh consent for THIS payment)
8. Guard: step-up requested AFTER a side effect (non-atomic tool)
• Baseline auth (401) and step-up (403) use the same challenge-driven client code (stepUpFetch).
• Tools never advertise the extra requirement; it is discovered during execution.
• Elicitation is UX (intent + "something is in course"), never the authorization itself.
• Atomic 403: a challenge is only allowed while nothing has been committed in the request.
• (Mcp-Session-Id, JSON-RPC id) identifies the pending operation across the replay.
• payment-op:<id> binds the stepped-up grant to ONE operation (Keycloak parameterized scope).
• Requires JSON response mode; client request timeout raised (5 min) for held requests.
